status_note: Reproduces on Polars 2.1.0, the latest release; `LogSeries::log` and `Expr.log` are unchanged on main (35a2cb73, 2026-11-04), read in the source. No matching issue found; [pola-rs/polars#23741](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/23741) (closed as not planned) is the related ulp discussion for division.
summary: `Expr.log()` on `Float32` computes `f32::log(x, base)` with the default base `math.e` cast to `Float32`, that is `ln(x) / ln(2.7182817)`, and `ln(2.7182817)` is 0.99999994 in single precision. So the natural logarithm of a `Float32` misses the correctly rounded value by an ulp for many inputs (`log(0.5)` is -0.69314724, numpy's `log` gives -0.6931472). `log10()` is `log(10.0)`, two roundings, also an ulp off (`log10(0.5)`). `Float64` is not affected for the natural log, since `ln(math.e)` rounds to 1.0.
handling: sverify does not work around it. `fp32` arithmetic is refused in every profile until #417's stage 3; a Polars profile that takes `fp32` must widen `fp.log` rounding or shim the natural log.
found_by: characterizing Polars against the formalization (characterization/polars/facts, round 2 source reading of `LogSeries::log`, then a manual repro)
